key_insight: CapNav exposes that Vision–Language Models for navigation must be conditioned on an agent’s mobility constraints — without capability conditioning, VLMs frequently recommend infeasible or unsafe routes. The benchmark measures how well models adapt navigation outputs to different embodied capabilities.
problem_solved: Closes the evaluation gap in VLN by providing a capability-conditioned benchmark that tests whether VLMs respect agent-specific mobility limits (e.g., stairs vs. ramps, narrow passages) during indoor navigation.
method: Define mobility capability profiles (e.g., wheeled, legged, low-clearance) and generate capability-aware navigation tasks and instructions in indoor environments.

Run standardized evaluations: feed VLMs the same linguistic prompts plus an explicit capability descriptor, execute navigation in simulation, and compute capability-conditioned metrics (success, path feasibility, efficiency).
Benchmark multiple VLMs and baselines, analyze failure modes, and evaluate simple conditioning/prompting strategies to measure improvement when models are capability-aware.
impact: Provides researchers and practitioners a practical protocol to audit and improve VLMs for embodied tasks, encouraging models that plan safely and feasibly for different robot types. Results guide dataset design, model conditioning, and deployment decisions in robotics and assistive applications.
visual_elements: Icon grid comparing agent types (wheeled, legged, vacuum, drone) with capability tags (stairs ✓/✗, narrow gap ✓/✗).
Pipeline diagram: instruction + capability profile → VLM decision → simulated trajectory → capability-conditioned metrics.
Heatmap or bar chart showing model performance across capability profiles (success rate / infeasible-action rate).
Example floorplan overlays with feasible vs. infeasible trajectories for different agents to illustrate failure cases.
paper_title: CapNav: Benchmarking Vision Language Models on Capability-conditioned Indoor Navigation
paper_authors: Xia Su, Ruiqi Chen, Benlin Liu, Jingwei Ma, Zonglin Di
